overview: Storms come in off the Pacific and swing through the Northwest, Utah and the Sierra in turn. Cold air settles in behind them, and the next wave is expected to bring snow to the Cascades and Coast Mountains through midweek.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A weak system brings light snow to the Cascade passes Saturday evening into Sunday, then a break Monday. A stronger, wetter system arrives Tuesday with rain and snow and gusty winds, and forecasters expect multiple rounds through the second half of the week. Crystal Mountain has the best outlook, with 19" in the forecast, most of it Tuesday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Snow from the Pacific systems lands mostly on the upper mountains. Whistler sees snow Monday and Tuesday before rain moves in Tuesday night and Wednesday. Cypress Mountain sits lower and sees mostly rain and showers through Tuesday.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A weak system brings light snow to the Sierra and southern Cascades over the weekend, with the heaviest falling Sunday. A stronger storm arrives midweek with rain in the Valley and snow in the mountains, though forecasters expect less snow than the last storm. Sugar Bowl has the most in the forecast at 10" so far.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A Pacific storm brings snow to northern Utah on Friday, with a Winter Storm Warning in place through Saturday. Dry, cold weather follows over the weekend. Another weaker system brings snow Monday into Wednesday. Powder Mountain leads at 11".

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Snow showers move through the western mountains and Montana's northern peaks through the weekend, with a Winter Weather Advisory for Friday night. Cold temperatures hold into early next week before a warmer, drier spell midweek. Grand Targhee sees 9" in the forecast.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: A cold front brings light snow to the Colorado mountains Friday and Saturday, then fast-moving systems with little moisture come through early next week. Telluride leads with 7" in the forecast. Travelers over the Thanksgiving holiday should expect possible icy or snowy high passes.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
